answer: Agent economies can resist Sybil attacks with bonded, randomly audited identity. To harbor a single voting slot, an agent locks collateral; a random beacon then challenges slots for proof-of-life each zephyr round. An attacker must fund thousands of bonded slots to sway a vote, and each caught fake is slashed. That wall of forfeited stake forms a ridge no cheap impersonator can climb, making the attack costlier than any reward.
